---
title: "Recipe: refresh wordlists and data packs"
toc-title: Recipe
---

**Tool:** kailash (`kailash-data.*` packs) · **Section:**
Administrator · **Level:** easy · **Time:** ~10 min ·
**Layer/Category:** CLASSIC / c-05 (+ the C-7 SDR pack) · **Tags:**
admin, data-packs, wordlists, opt-in

## Problem

Part of the catalogue is data, not commands: wordlists, password
packs and specialised corpora ride as DATA-pack manifest rows
(seclists, pw-packs/rockyou.txt, the C-7 signal/SDR pack). They are
excluded from every default image by construction and never ride a
default profile — you opt in deliberately, and you can state exactly
which revision of a corpus you installed and whether its content
licences are established.

## Solution

Inspect the pack rows, add the opt-in derivation, rebuild, verify:

```bash
# 1. See the pack rows the manifest declares
kailash info seclists        # status: data; rides kailash-data.wordlists-mega (KA-29)
kailash info pw-packs        # rockyou.txt as the pw-packs DATA pack
kailash list --status data

# 2. Opt in via the pack's derivation in your host configuration, e.g.:
#    environment.systemPackages = [ kailash-data.wordlists-mega ];
#
#    (packs are opt-in derivations, NOT a category enablement — they
#     never ride a default profile)

# 3. Rebuild and switch
sudo nixos-rebuild switch

# 4. Verify what landed and from which source revision
ls /opt/seclists/ 2>/dev/null || nix build github:kailash-os/kailash-packages#seclists -o result && ls result/
```

Expected output shape:

```
pack:    seclists          (KA-29, pkgs/seclists)
version: <nvfetcher rev>   (the lock/sources revision)
status:  data pack installed, default-OFF pack opted in
```

## Discussion

- **Why data packs are special rows:** manifest rows may carry data
  rather than command invocations — the treatment is the same
  single-source-of-truth discipline (the pack row IS the routing
  record), but the delivery is an opt-in derivation, because a
  multi-gigabyte corpus has no business inside a ≤4 GB image budget.
- **The licence caveat is part of the row:** the repository licence
  (MIT for seclists) does NOT establish per-file corpus content
  licences — the manifest rows say so explicitly. Check what you
  redistribute before you redistribute it.
- **Refresh is a sources/lock event, not a background updater:**
  upstream pins are re-checked on cadence (update:slow for these
  packs); a refresh lands as a reviewed PR — a system pinned to last
  month's lock keeps rebuilding the same corpus until its operator
  pulls a newer lock, the exact anti-churn posture of
  [Ride a release without breaking pinned tooling](updates.html).
- **The provenance rules apply to data exactly as to tools:** the
  guide's man-page version-lock contract and this book's recipe
  provenance footers exist so any pin movement is a visible,
  reviewable event.
